findings.issue_text: Installer-identity check only runs when an Integration row exists; on Integration.DoesNotExist the pipeline advances with no check, so anyone knowing an installation_id can claim it during the webhook race (should fail closed or verify sender via get_installation_info())

integration.metadata["sender"]["login"] raises KeyError for integrations whose metadata lacks a sender block, producing a 500 instead of the error page; should use .get() chains and treat missing sender as mismatch

OAuth state uses pipeline.signature, a deterministic value identical across runs for the same org/provider, so it provides no replay protection and leaked authorize URLs remain valid indefinitely; should bind a random per-request nonce
State comparison request.GET.get("state") != pipeline.signature is non-constant-time for a secret-derived value; should use django.utils.crypto.constant_time_compare

Integration.objects.get(external_id=installation_id, status=ACTIVE) does not filter on provider="github", so a collision with another provider (e.g. github_enterprise) can raise MultipleObjectsReturned or match the wrong integration; the pre-existing lookup above has the same gap
redirect_uri and state are interpolated into the authorize URL without urlencode, so ?, &, or # in the absolute URI corrupts the query string; should build with urllib.parse.urlencode
On OAuth denial (?error=access_denied), code is None but the view still POSTs to the token endpoint before showing a generic error; should check for code/error up front and short-circuit

test_installation_not_found no longer tests the not-found path; it now only exercises a state mismatch, leaving the Integration-exists-but-not-ACTIVE case untested and the state-mismatch case without a correctly named test
No test coverage for token-exchange failure (no access_token in response) or for /user returning no login, both new error branches

Tests hardcode the literal signature 9cae5e88803f35ed7970fc131e6e65d3, so any change to SECRET_KEY, signing scheme, or fixture IDs breaks every setup test opaquely; should read pipeline.signature or parse it from the redirect

adjudication_records.issue_text: OAuth state uses pipeline.signature, a deterministic value identical across runs for the same org/provider, so it provides no replay protection and leaked authorize URLs remain valid indefinitely; should bind a random per-request nonce
matched_golden_ids: OAuth state uses pipeline.signature (static) instead of a per-request random value
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: The candidate issue flags that OAuth state is set to pipeline.signature, which is deterministic/static and should be a per-request random nonce to prevent replay—this is the same underlying problem as the golden comment.

adjudication_records.issue_text: State comparison request.GET.get("state") != pipeline.signature is non-constant-time for a secret-derived value; should use django.utils.crypto.constant_time_compare

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a `state` check: `if request.GET.get("state") != pipeline.signature:`. While this is a normal string comparison (not constant-time), the finding hinges on `pipeline.signature` being a *secret-derived* value where timing leaks are meaningful. That is not verifiable from this diff: we can’t confirm how `pipeline.signature` is constructed, and in OAuth the `state` value is typically a random token sent to the client (not a server-secret being protected from timing attacks). Thus the claim of a real, demonstrable security defect introduced by the diff is not supported by the shown changes.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Integration.objects.get(external_id=installation_id, status=ACTIVE) does not filter on provider="github", so a collision with another provider (e.g. github_enterprise) can raise MultipleObjectsReturned or match the wrong integration; the pre-existing lookup above has the same gap

adjudication.rationale: In `GitHubInstallation.dispatch`, the code performs `Integration.objects.get(external_id=installation_id)` (for `installations_exist`) and later `Integration.objects.get(external_id=installation_id, status=ObjectStatus.ACTIVE)` without constraining `provider`. Since `Integration` is a shared table across providers, it is plausible/typical that `external_id` is only unique per-provider (e.g., `unique_together(provider, external_id)`), meaning the same `external_id` could exist for another provider (including `github_enterprise`). In that case, these `.get()` calls can either raise `MultipleObjectsReturned` (unhandled here) or retrieve an integration for the wrong provider, causing incorrect behavior. The diff does not add the earlier lookup, but it does add a new `.get()` with the same missing provider filter, so the finding matches a real correctness risk present in the changed code.

adjudication_records.issue_text: redirect_uri and state are interpolated into the authorize URL without urlencode, so ?, &, or # in the absolute URI corrupts the query string; should build with urllib.parse.urlencode

adjudication.rationale: In OAuthLoginView.dispatch, the authorize URL is built via f-string: `...?client_id=...&state=...&redirect_uri={redirect_uri}`. However, in this diff `redirect_uri` is produced by `absolute_uri(reverse("sentry-extension-setup", ...))`, which is a fixed path without any query string or fragment, and the added/updated tests assert it is exactly `http://testserver/extensions/github/setup/`. Characters like `:` and `/` in `redirect_uri` do not corrupt the surrounding query string, and `state` is a hex signature. The finding’s scenario (redirect_uri containing `?`, `&`, or `#`) is not evidenced or reasonably implied by the diff, so it’s not a verifiable defect introduced here (though using `urlencode` would be more robust stylistically).

adjudication_records.issue_text: On OAuth denial (?error=access_denied), code is None but the view still POSTs to the token endpoint before showing a generic error; should check for code/error up front and short-circuit

adjudication.rationale: In `OAuthLoginView.dispatch`, once `state` is present and matches, it unconditionally builds `data = {"code": request.GET.get("code"), ...}` and immediately calls `safe_urlopen(..., data=data)` to exchange for a token. There is no guard for the OAuth denial case (`?error=access_denied`), nor even a check that `code` is present/non-empty before posting to the token endpoint. On denial, `code` will be `None`, so the view still performs the token POST and only afterward returns the generic `error(...)` when `access_token` is missing. This matches the proposed finding and is a concrete behavior in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: test_installation_not_found no longer tests the not-found path; it now only exercises a state mismatch, leaving the Integration-exists-but-not-ACTIVE case untested and the state-mismatch case without a correctly named test

adjudication.rationale: In the diff, `test_installation_not_found` was changed from asserting the "The GitHub installation could not be found." content to instead performing an OAuth callback request with a hard-coded `state` (`ddd0...`) that does not match the pipeline signature used elsewhere (`9cae...`) and then asserting "Invalid installation request.". That means the test no longer exercises an installation-not-found scenario and is effectively a state-mismatch/invalid-request test with an incorrect name. Also, the new production code introduces a stricter lookup `Integration.objects.get(external_id=installation_id, status=ObjectStatus.ACTIVE)` and errors on `DoesNotExist`, which includes the "exists but not ACTIVE" case; there is no corresponding test added in the diff that targets that new branch.

adjudication_records.issue_text: No test coverage for token-exchange failure (no access_token in response) or for /user returning no login, both new error branches

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces two new early-error branches in `OAuthLoginView.dispatch`: returning `error(...)` when the token exchange response payload lacks `access_token`, and returning `error(...)` when `get_user_info(...)` does not include a `login`. The added tests and `_stub_github` always stub a successful token exchange (`body="access_token=..."`) and `/user` response with `{"login": "octocat"}`, and the new/updated tests cover state mismatch, installation not found, and user mismatch against `integration.metadata["sender"]["login"]`, but they do not exercise either of these two new failure branches. So the finding accurately identifies missing test coverage introduced by this change.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Tests hardcode the literal signature 9cae5e88803f35ed7970fc131e6e65d3, so any change to SECRET_KEY, signing scheme, or fixture IDs breaks every setup test opaquely; should read pipeline.signature or parse it from the redirect

adjudication.rationale: In the updated tests, multiple assertions and follow-up requests hardcode the OAuth `state` value `9cae5e88803f35ed7970fc131e6e65d3` (e.g., `assert redirect.query == "client_id=...&state=9cae..."` and later GETs include `state` with that literal). In the code change, `state` is set to `pipeline.signature`, which is not defined in the test itself and is derived from pipeline/signing behavior. This makes the tests brittle: any change to how `pipeline.signature` is produced (signing scheme, key, pipeline construction) will break these tests even if behavior is still correct. The issue is directly present in the diff (new hardcoded state usage).
